{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent history, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.",
    "If model shows steady upward trend with no recent spike, but true outcome shows sharp drop, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% to account for mean reversion.",
    "After a model forecast spike (e.g., >+3% from prior), reduce subsequent forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overshoot.",
    "When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.1), model often overpredicts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean.",
    "If true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days, assume lagged reaction; adjust forecast to align with 3rd–5th day true values for next 7 days.",
    "If sentiment history shows repeated 0.2–0.4 spikes, model tends to overreact; cap forecast growth at 0.8% per day after spike.",
    "For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early volatility (first 5 days), model often misses it; use sentiment to weight early days more heavily in forecast."
  ]
}
